newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany shares pulled down after UK rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Germany shares pulled down after UK rate hike.

text.p: German shares ended Wednesday's bourse trade slightly higher, but at the day's low point, after the dollar slipped and German bonds lost some sheen following the surprise raising of the UK interest rate.
The DAX index of 30 blue-chip shares closed up 5.11 points, or 0.19 percent, at 2,678.73, slipping back about ten points after Britain raised its base interest rate by 25 basis points to six percent.
German players took the move as a signal that German interest rates would not sink further in the future and the DAX fell in IBIS electronic trade.

Later, the bond markets suffered after higher-than-forecast U.S. GDP and new homes data, which combined with a weaker dollar and the IBIS DAX index ended down 10.78 points, or 0.40 percent, at 2,664.72.

The most heavily traded stock during computer dealings was German's largest commercial bank, Deutsche Bank, which ended IBIS trade up five pfennigs at 70.40 marks, after news management board member Rolf Breuer would succeed Hilmar Kopper as chief executive.
The banking sector was generally stronger, except Dresdner Bank, which reports its nine month results on Thursday and ended the day down 21 pfennigs at 40.69 marks.

Meanwhile shares in carmaker Volkswagen ignored news that German courts had dismissed its law suit against Opel, a unit of U.S. firm General Motors. VW shares ended computer trade up 4.50 marks at 598 marks.
